chunks: Li-ion chemistry in consumer electronics. The question: What is the common battery chemistry used in rechargeable consumer electronics? Why?
Almost every phone, laptop and power tool uses a lithium-ion battery. It is a rechargeable battery that packs a lot of stored energy into a small, light package.
This page asks why it won, and the answer is a handful of measurable advantages, plus the price you pay for them.
Think of choosing a backpack for a long hike. You want the most food (energy) for the least weight and space, and you want it to stay fresh in the bag.
Lithium-ion is the lightweight pack that carries the most food and keeps it fresh.
The catch is that it needs careful handling, and a rip in the bag is more serious than with a plain canvas sack.
The hyperbola shows why the first factor of 2-3 in density matters so much for handheld devices.
A phone-sized 15 watt hours battery is about 60 g in Li-ion and several hundred grams in older chemistries. The marked densities are representative values, not specific products.
Energy density: how much energy a battery stores per kilogram or per liter, in Wh/kg or Wh/L ("Desirable battery characteristics").
Nominal voltage: the typical voltage while in use. A lithium-ion cell is about 3. 7 volts; a nickel cell is 1. 2 volts. Self-discharge: charge a battery loses just sitting unused.
Memory effect: a loss of usable capacity in some old nickel batteries if you recharge them partly used. Lithium-ion has almost none.
Lithium polymer (LiPo): a lithium-ion cell in a flat pouch instead of a metal can ("What LiPo stands for").
Suppose a phone needs 15 watt hours of stored energy. A lithium-ion cell at about 250 watt hours/kg would weigh 15 / 250 = 0. 06 kg, or 60 g.
A NiMH cell at about 90 watt hours/kg would weigh about 167 g. A lead-acid battery at about 35 watt hours/kg would weigh over 400 g. Nobody wants that in a pocket.
"Lithium-ion, packaged as lithium polymer pouch cells in phones and wearables, and as cylindrical cells like the 18650 in laptops and tools.
The reasons: much higher energy density, two to three times NiMH and many times lead-acid; a 3.
7 volts cell so one cell can run the electronics; low self-discharge; no memory effect; good power and cycle life. The cost is a charger, protection circuit and safety care."
